scope: 100 R-134a imported designs; local metadata revision only
visualMethod: All 100 full-page thumbnails inspected on the five supplied contact sheets. Numeric table rows, units, page dimensions and original checksums checked separately against the native PDFs and canonical data. Contact-sheet inspection does not certify every individual printed glyph.
designStructure: Five data editions reused across design families; distinct titles describe visual differences, not 100 independent datasets.

items.observation: A turquoise refrigerant cylinder stands on a white pedestal beside the blue heading, above two blocks of saturation data.
items.title: R-134a US Overview Chart — Blue Cylinder Header
items.summary: A turquoise refrigerant cylinder stands on a white pedestal beside the blue heading, above two blocks of saturation data.
descriptionParagraphs: Use this chart to look up the saturation pressure of R-134a from a Fahrenheit temperature, then compare the equivalent Celsius reading on the same row. The 5°F spacing gives a broad overview rather than the finer steps of the detailed edition. This blue cylinder header version covers -40 to 180°F in 5°F steps.
The rounded heading leaves the reference table in its own white panel, separate from the equipment illustration. The 45 listed reference points use Fahrenheit, Celsius, psi gauge, bar gauge.

items.observation: A yellow contact thermometer sits in a raised white panel within the orange heading, with Celsius-led columns underneath.
items.title: R-134a SI Overview Chart — Orange Thermometer Header
items.summary: A yellow contact thermometer sits in a raised white panel within the orange heading, with Celsius-led columns underneath.
descriptionParagraphs: Start with the Celsius column to find an R-134a saturation temperature, then read across for the equivalent Fahrenheit temperature and pressure. Its 2°C spacing is useful when you want a broad metric reference on one sheet. This orange thermometer header version covers -40 to 80°C in 2°C steps.
The rounded heading leaves the reference table in its own white panel, separate from the equipment illustration. The 61 listed reference points use Celsius, Fahrenheit, bar gauge, kPa absolute.

items.summary: A cylinder photograph and small pedestal anchor the magenta header above a fine-step Fahrenheit table.
descriptionParagraphs: This chart gives a closer-spaced view of the R-134a pressure-temperature relationship, using 2°F increments. Follow a Fahrenheit row across to compare its Celsius equivalent with both gauge pressure and absolute pressure in psi. This magenta cylinder header version covers 0 to 120°F in 2°F steps.
The rounded heading leaves the reference table in its own white panel, separate from the equipment illustration. The 61 listed reference points use Fahrenheit, Celsius, psi gauge, psi absolute.

items.summary: A silver dial sits above a magenta saturation curve, with two overview table blocks below the graph.
descriptionParagraphs: Use this chart to look up the saturation pressure of R-134a from a Fahrenheit temperature, then compare the equivalent Celsius reading on the same row. The 5°F spacing gives a broad overview rather than the finer steps of the detailed edition. This magenta gauge and curve version covers -40 to 180°F in 5°F steps.

The small curve shows the overall pressure-temperature trend; use the table below it to read the listed values for individual reference points. The 45 listed reference points use Fahrenheit, Celsius, psi gauge, bar gauge.

descriptionParagraphs: Start with the Celsius column to find an R-134a saturation temperature, then read across for the equivalent Fahrenheit temperature and pressure. Its 2°C spacing is useful when you want a broad metric reference on one sheet. This copper molecule and curve version covers -40 to 80°C in 2°C steps.

The small curve shows the overall pressure-temperature trend; use the table below it to read the listed values for individual reference points. The 61 listed reference points use Celsius, Fahrenheit, bar gauge, kPa absolute.

items.summary: A thermometer photograph and reference values sit in the navy right column beside three Celsius overview blocks.
descriptionParagraphs: Start with the Celsius column to find an R-134a saturation temperature, then read across for the equivalent Fahrenheit temperature and pressure. Its 2°C spacing is useful when you want a broad metric reference on one sheet. This blue thermometer landscape version covers -40 to 80°C in 2°C steps.
The equipment and reference-state panel sits on the right, leaving the landscape table together on the left. The 61 listed reference points use Celsius, Fahrenheit, bar gauge, kPa absolute.

items.observation: A yellow thermometer sits in the orange right sidebar, next to three blocks of detailed Fahrenheit readings.
items.title: R-134a US Detailed Chart — Orange Thermometer Landscape
items.summary: A yellow thermometer sits in the orange right sidebar, next to three blocks of detailed Fahrenheit readings.
descriptionParagraphs: This chart gives a closer-spaced view of the R-134a pressure-temperature relationship, using 2°F increments. Follow a Fahrenheit row across to compare its Celsius equivalent with both gauge pressure and absolute pressure in psi. This orange thermometer landscape version covers 0 to 120°F in 2°F steps.
The equipment and reference-state panel sits on the right, leaving the landscape table together on the left. The 61 listed reference points use Fahrenheit, Celsius, psi gauge, psi absolute.

items.observation: A white thermometer card and reference-state values occupy the magenta right strip beside detailed Celsius data.
items.title: R-134a SI Detailed Chart — Magenta Thermometer Landscape
items.summary: A white thermometer card and reference-state values occupy the magenta right strip beside detailed Celsius data.
descriptionParagraphs: Use this sheet when you need an R-134a reference at 1°C intervals. Read across a Celsius row to compare gauge pressure in bar with absolute pressure in kPa; those pressure columns use different reference points. This magenta thermometer landscape version covers -20 to 60°C in 1°C steps.
The equipment and reference-state panel sits on the right, leaving the landscape table together on the left. The 81 listed reference points use Celsius, bar gauge, kPa absolute.

items.observation: A grayscale vessel labeled for vapor and liquid sits in the right sidebar beside the pressure lookup table.
items.title: R-134a Pressure Lookup Chart — Grayscale Vessel Landscape
items.summary: A grayscale vessel labeled for vapor and liquid sits in the right sidebar beside the pressure lookup table.
descriptionParagraphs: This version starts with gauge pressure rather than temperature. Find a listed psig value, then read across for the matching R-134a saturation temperature in Fahrenheit and Celsius; the 5-psi spacing makes the pressure steps easy to follow. This grayscale vessel landscape version covers 0 to 200 psig in 5-psi steps.
The equipment and reference-state panel sits on the right, leaving the landscape table together on the left. The 41 listed reference points use psi gauge, Fahrenheit, Celsius.
